title: SSH Trust and Connection Setup
objective: Prepare secure, repeatable SSH access from a control node to managed nodes.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 02 - SSH Overview & Setup
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Ansible usually transports module work over SSH, so connection reliability comes before playbooks. The controller must know the remote host, login user, authentication method, and host-key policy.

A public key may be installed on each managed node while its private half remains protected on the controller. An SSH agent can hold an unlocked key temporarily, avoiding repeated passphrase prompts without removing key protection.

Troubleshoot SSH directly before blaming Ansible. Confirm addressing, username, key permissions, host-key verification, and a successful interactive login, then test the same details through inventory.
explanation.rule: If plain SSH cannot connect reliably, Ansible will not connect reliably either.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
ssh_access:
  user: ansible
  authentication: public_key
  private_key_mode: "0600"
  password_login: disabled
  root_login: disabled

lab.title: Trace the lab connection
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Inspect the inventory variables used for the training connection.
lab.verify: ssh -o BatchMode=yes ansible@web01 hostname; ansible webservers -m ansible.builtin.ping
lab.success: Direct SSH reaches web01 and Ansible returns pong from both webservers.
